title: Full four-language representation and transformation; default CST support for all languages
body:
## Maintainer clarification — full support is required (2026-09-23)

> There should be no limitations. Meta language must fully support representation and transformation of all the requested languages, and all the existing languages as CST by default.

The required result is **full representation and transformation of JavaScript, Rust, Rocq/Coq and Lean, plus complete lossless CSTs by default for all existing languages**, with equivalent capabilities in JavaScript and Rust. The current repository language inventory is a minimum coverage audit, not a cap on this requirement.

The [detailed acceptance clarification and reproduced gaps on PR #196](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5795832509) is part of this issue's requirements and must be added to the committed requirement ledger.

- [ ] Deliver grammar-level CSTs through the normal parse API for every language, including existing dialects, aliases and embedded-language paths. Generic text, token streams and delimiter groups do not satisfy CST support.
- [ ] Deliver complete structured representation and transformation for the four requested languages, including bindings/scopes, project context, modules, types, macros/notation and proof/tactic syntax; support structured construction, edits and source generation.
- [ ] Implement the 12 directed cross-language translations already requested, with explicit preservation contracts and tested faithful encodings. Unsupported descriptors are unfinished work, not completed translations.
- [ ] Verify all capabilities using shared JS/Rust grammar and transformation corpora, real projects, negative cases and actual published packages. Do not lower parity to the weaker implementation or remove languages/constructs to pass coverage.
- [ ] Complete the implementation in PR #196, retain every earlier requirement below, and keep this issue open until delivery evidence exists. Do not treat a documented intermediate subset as completion.

This clarification supersedes any interpretation of the original wording that permits permanent omissions or unsupported/opaque capability reports to count as delivered full support. During implementation, diagnostics and status reports must remain truthful; marking a limitation as documented does not resolve it.

## Original request and evidence

RML needs complete, editable representations of JavaScript, Rust, Rocq, and Lean supplied by `meta-language`, with the same observable contracts in its JavaScript and Rust packages. This is an upstream dependency request from the review of [relative-meta-logic PR #184](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/pull/184), following the maintainer's [four-language requirement](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/pull/184#issuecomment-5773514118).

The requested result is structured language representation and translation infrastructure. RML will own its logic, proof checking, execution semantics, selectable foundations, and RML-specific language extension. Generic concepts shared by languages should live here when their meanings actually coincide.

## Verified gaps, 2026-09-23

Reviewed meta-language main at `922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664` (source version 0.58.2), and RML PR head `c24f5b98cc2f6bce2145993d7a1a6b03f2e67122`.

1. [`js/src/network.js:27`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664/js/src/network.js#L27) handles `lino` specially and routes other languages through `parseLosslessText`. `_indexJavaScriptIdentifiers` uses a regular expression, not a JavaScript parser. Rust/Lean/Rocq inputs produce source-token links without language syntax structure. Text preservation alone does not establish language support.
2. [`rust/src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs:141`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664/rust/src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs#L141) has JavaScript and Rust grammar dispatch, but no Lean/Rocq/Coq dispatch. The [built-in parser](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664/rust/src/language_parser.rs) silently falls back to lossless text for those languages. Thus the two runtimes also provide different syntax capabilities.
3. [`parity/language-features.json`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664/parity/language-features.json) explicitly exempts the Rust language-parser modules from JavaScript parity. Passing the present parity manifest therefore does not establish four-language parser parity.
4. npm still reports only `meta-language@0.46.0` (`npm view meta-language dist-tags versions --json`), while source and the [latest release](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/releases/tag/v0.58.2) are 0.58.2. RML consequently consumes npm 0.46.0 and Rust 0.58.2. This reproduces the release-distribution concern of closed [#171](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/171); a fix present only in main is not available out of the box to downstream users.

I ran the following on current meta-language source after `cd js && npm ci --ignore-scripts`:

```js
import { LinkNetwork, LinkQuery, ReplacementRule } from './src/index.js';

const source = 'const x = 1; const s = "x"; // x\n';
const network = LinkNetwork.parse(source, 'JavaScript');
const query = LinkQuery.fromSexpression('(identifier) @target\n(#eq? @target "x")');
const matches = network.find(query);
network.replace(matches, ReplacementRule.capturedText('target', 'y'));
console.log(matches.length, network.reconstructText());
```

Actual: three matches and `const y = 1; const s = "y"; // y`. Expected for an identifier-only query: one match, with the string literal and comment preserved. The same failure occurs through RML's published-dependency adapter.

Other current JS-source probes all reconstruct their input exactly, but `fn id(x: u64) -> u64 { x }`, `def id (x : Nat) : Nat := x`, and `Definition id (x : nat) : nat := x.` have only `SourceToken` links. `const x = 1;` has 12 source-token links and one regex-created `Syntax` identifier link, not a full JavaScript syntax tree.

## Acceptance requirements

- [ ] Ship registered parsers and emitters for JavaScript, Rust, Rocq (including the Coq alias), and Lean in both runtime packages. Declare exact supported language versions/editions and extensions, and inventory every language construct against implementation and conformance evidence. Retain the full-coverage requirement; a supported subset is an intermediate state, not completion.
- [ ] Preserve complete source bytes/trivia, syntax hierarchy, identifiers and scope/binding, module/import references, declarations, types/universes, recursive bodies, attributes/macros/notation, effects, and proof/tactic syntax where applicable. Distinguish parsed, resolved, elaborated, and opaque representations. Unknown syntax and unavailable plugins must be reported explicitly, with their source retained; fallback text must never be labelled successful semantic parsing.
- [ ] Provide language-independent links for genuinely shared concepts, with lossless language-specific extensions for differing meanings. Do not equate similar spellings, collapse proof universes, invent compatible effects, or discard unsupported information.
- [ ] Support structured edits and source generation after the original source buffer is unavailable. Add binding-aware rename/capture tests, including identifiers in strings/comments, shadowing, Unicode, nested scopes, macros/notation and invalid input.
- [ ] Expose a stable parse → network → transform → emit contract, fidelity/capability reports, provenance/source mappings, schema versioning and extension registration. Keep RML-specific syntax and proof/foundation policy in RML; make only reusable binding, typing, module, proof-syntax and translation concepts shared here.
- [ ] Supply the common representation and translation hooks needed for all 12 directed pairs among the four languages. Define each translation's observation/semantic-preservation contract, required runtime/encoding and assumptions. Preserve non-native constructs through an explicit supported encoding or return a precise unsupported obligation. Passing text through under a new language label, translating a keyword, or silently weakening a theorem does not count as a translation.
- [ ] Keep source preservation, syntax coverage, semantic lowering, emitted-code validity and behavior/proof preservation as separately tested capabilities. Native compilers/provers may validate emitted artifacts; their success alone does not prove the translation correct or supply RML's internal reasoning authority.
- [ ] Run one shared conformance corpus through both runtime packages, checking normalized links, scopes, diagnostics, reconstruction, mutations and translation results. Remove capability exemptions that conceal these parser gaps. Include corpus-derived negative cases and integration tests consumed by RML.
- [ ] Publish matching usable npm/crates releases and demonstrate installation and the four-language examples from those published artifacts. Resolve or explicitly link the continuing #171 publication problem rather than requiring downstream consumers to pin an unpublished npm version.

Existing closed work on parser registries ([#52](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/52)), shared concepts ([#57](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/57)), translation registries ([#58](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/58)), recursive translation ([#183](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/183)), and grammar translation ([#112](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/112)) provides infrastructure to reuse. It does not demonstrate these four complete language implementations or their cross-language fidelity.

Please keep this request open until the coverage and published-package evidence exists. RML's downstream audit should link the implementing PRs, release versions and integration tests; opening this issue itself is not completion of downstream language support.
